newsitem.title: UK: Euro, Asia refinery maintenance lighter in '97 -IEA.
newsitem.headline: Euro, Asia refinery maintenance lighter in '97 -IEA.

text.p: Spring maintenance programmes at European and Asian refineries are expected to be lighter this year than the last three years, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
Spring maintenance programmes are currently peaking in Europe and are on the rise in Asia.
In Europe, turnarounds are expected to claim 890,000 barrels per day (bpd) of primary distillation capacity in May, 810,000 in June and 250,000 in July.
Maintenance at refineries in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to close down 600,000 bpd in May, 650,000 bpd in June and 350,000 bpd in July.
U.S. refineries have largely emerged from the maintenance season and turnarounds are expected to affect just 170,000 bpd and 190,000 bpd in May and June respectively.

But maintenance programmes are not set in stone, the IEA noted, with the timing and extent of turnarounds likely to be influenced by Atlantic basin gasoline markets, Asian distillate markets and weather conditions.

IEA figures for March show aggregate refinery throughputs in OECD countries down by 800,000 bpd to 32.3 million bpd, with increases in the U.S. more than offset by decreases in Europe, Japan, Canada and Australasia.
The IEA estimated that throughput levels in April increased in the U.S. and decreased in Japan and Europe.
